claim: A 1966 period tire survey distinguished Firestone F100 radial products from Sports 130 cross-ply nylon racing-compound products, showing that construction architecture and compound category cannot be inferred from brand alone.
provenanceLocation: The Latest in Tyres, manufacturer survey

claim: The same period survey documented simultaneous road, high-speed and competition-oriented product families across Firestone, Goodyear and other suppliers.
provenanceLocation: The Latest in Tyres, product survey
applicability: Catalogue/menu architecture; no numerical physics transfer.

claim: A 1968 period report described increasingly wide tires on sports prototypes as a visible development direction.
Under unusually hot 1959 Reims conditions, the period report noted no tire changes in the Grand Prix and Formula 2 races and described Dunlop as used by nearly all competitors.
applicability: Event-specific durability and supplier context; not a universal wear curve.

claim: Dunlop's official retrospective identifies the 1959 RS5 racing tire with a nylon casing and safety-shoulder feature.
applicability: RS5 nomenclature and construction history only; preserve the source's RS5 spelling.

claim: Modern Dunlop vintage-racing guidance varies recommended cold and hot pressures materially by vehicle weight and tire family, including Vintage/R5, L-section, M-section, Post Historic and Group C constructions.
provenanceLocation: Dunlop Vintage Racing Tire Pressure Guide, pressure table
applicability: Modern reproduction-tire setup architecture only; not original-period pressure evidence.

claim: The modern guide recommends front/rear pressure bias according to front- versus rear-engine load distribution and using pressure changes to tune handling balance.
provenanceLocation: Dunlop Vintage Racing Tire Pressure Guide, setup notes
applicability: Modern reproduction-racing setup method; no historical coefficient transfer.

claim: The 1996 IMSA GTS regulations provide primary sanction-specific wheel/tire configuration constraints but do not document operating pressure, temperature, stiffness or wear.
applicability: 1996 IMSA GTS fitment and acquisition routing.

claim: Mitsubishi's official 1993 WRC history records a minimum-weight increase from 1100 to 1200 kg and a maximum tire-diameter reduction from 680 to 650 mm for that regulation context.
applicability: 1993 WRC regulation/vehicle context; no tire operating data.

claim: FIA Appendix K supplies authoritative current historic-category definitions and tire eligibility rules, but current historic rules must be separated from evidence of original-period race practice.
applicability: Ontology and modern historic regulation only.

claim: Porsche's official retrospective places the 956/962 in the Group C chronology beginning in 1982.
Dunlop's official 1982 history associates its motorsport activity with the opening Group C/Porsche 956 period.
The 2021 Dunlop vintage catalogue provides current reproduction-tire dimensions and applications that can be used as a fitment cross-check only when clearly labeled as modern reproduction data.
provenanceLocation: Dunlop Vintage Racing Tire Dimensions and Applications
